messages:
jamal: Hey — seeing intermittent 401s for customers on the /v1/stream endpoint. Happens only when the request goes through their proxy. Two sample request IDs from logs: req-4a7c9d2 and req-4a7c9d9. No obvious rate limit spike. Anyone can help assemble a minimal curl we can give them to repro?

support-bot: Thanks for the IDs, jamal. Can you paste the exact request headers (redact secrets) + the short trace log around the error? Also indicate if SSE cut off immediately or after a few tokens. :eyes:

jamal: headers (redacted):
  Authorization: REDACTED
  Accept: text/event-stream
  User-Agent: client/1.2.3
  X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3
  X-Request-Id: req-4a7c9d2
Logs show: 
  2026-03-12T14:22:11Z INFO incoming /v1/stream req=req-4a7c9d2 auth=passed
  2026-03-12T14:22:11Z WARN proxy-response 401 from upstream for req-4a7c9d2
SSE cutoff: immediate (no events delivered).

alex: Quick minimal curl to try (replace $TOKEN and $URL):

  curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    -H "X-Request-Id: req-4a7c9d2" 
    "$URL/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat-1"

Use --no-buffer so you see streaming behavior. If proxy is altering headers, try adding --header "Connection: keep-alive" as well.

maria: Also check if the proxy strips or rewrites Authorization or x-* headers. Ask customer to run this exact curl and paste the full verbose (-v) output. If they can't share token, ask them to send the curl -v output but replace the token with <REDACTED>.

sophia: If they see 401 from upstream, capture both sides: local curl -v and the proxy access log entry for that request id. To collect a compact debug bundle ask for: request id, curl -v dump, proxy access log lines, and the timestamp window +/- 1 minute. That usually is enough to find header mangling.

jamal: Cool — I'll get the customer to run the curl snippet and send back the -v output + proxy logs. One extra thing: they mentioned intermittent success when they retry w/ same TCP connection. Could be keep-alive / connection pooling causing auth header to drop on reused connection.

alex: Good note. If they can reproduce reliably, ask them to test with: 

  curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$URL/v1/stream?model=redwood-chat-1"

Forcing HTTP/1.1 rules out some HTTP/2 intermediary behavior.

maria: If they provide the curl output, include it in the ticket and I can correlate with our server logs for req-4a7c9d2/req-4a7c9d9. If we confirm proxy mangling, we can advise the customer to preserve headers or use a signed header scheme. :+1:

jamal: Sending checklist to customer now. Will update here with the curl -v dump and proxy logs when I get them. Thanks all! :pray:
